meta.title: Thiscloud UI — Center Aurora documentation
meta.footerSupport: Web/hybrid RC API · local assets only

explore.title: Build interfaces from a clear component language.
explore.intro: Start with purpose, compare categories, then inspect component states and accessibility contracts. Core information stays visible.
explore.browseIntro: Distinct previews make each family recognizable before you read.

category.intro: components with purpose, truthful previews, and direct references.

component.accessibilityText: Use a semantic name, visible focus, keyboard activation, and state text. This component remains operable without pointer input.
component.demoOnly: No public SDK API: this route is a design demo.
component.demoCodeBoundary: No public SDK code is provided for this design demo.

Button.anatomy: Native button, visible label, intent styling, focus ring, and optional disabled or loading state.
Button.usage: Use one clear action per context; choose emphasis by intent and keep its label stable while it works.
Button.api: TcButton exposes label, type, variant, disabled, loading, and callbacks through tc.ui.button.
Button.accessibility: Use type=button, name, visible focus, and disabled when unavailable; Enter and Space activate.

ButtonFab.anatomy: Circular or extended button, meaningful icon, accessible name, focus ring, and disabled state.
ButtonFab.usage: Use for a high-value contextual action; prefer an extended label when the icon is unfamiliar.
ButtonFab.api: TcButtonFab exposes icon, label, extended, variant, disabled, and callbacks through tc.ui.button-fab.
ButtonFab.accessibility: Every icon-only control has a name, native target, visible focus, and real disabled state.

ButtonGroup.anatomy: Named group, related native buttons, shared boundary, coherent tab order, and wrapped layout.
ButtonGroup.usage: Group actions that share a context; keep each action understandable and avoid toolbar behavior.
ButtonGroup.api: TcButtonGroup exposes group label, ordered actions, selection, orientation, and wrapping.
ButtonGroup.accessibility: Name the group; keep native buttons in DOM order without roving focus or toolbar semantics.

IconButton.anatomy: Native button, action icon, stable accessible name, focus ring, and 40px target.
IconButton.usage: Use for a compact, familiar action; pair unfamiliar icons with visible context.
IconButton.api: TcIconButton exposes icon, label, variant, disabled, and callbacks through tc.ui.icon-button.
IconButton.accessibility: Name every icon-only button; keep focus visible and use disabled when unavailable.

ToggleIconButton.anatomy: Native button, stable name, aria-pressed state, focus ring, and live status.
ToggleIconButton.usage: Use when one action has two persistent states; keep its accessible label stable.
ToggleIconButton.api: TcToggleIconButton exposes icon, label, pressed, disabled, and callbacks via tc.ui.toggle-icon-button.
ToggleIconButton.accessibility: Keep the action name stable, expose aria-pressed as false or true, and announce state changes.

Toolbar.anatomy: Named toolbar, horizontal orientation, enabled command buttons, roving tabindex, and status output.
Toolbar.usage: Group frequent peer commands; let Tab enter and leave while Left and Right move within the toolbar.
Toolbar.api: TcToolbar exposes label, orientation, actions, disabled items, wrapping, callbacks via tc.ui.toolbar.
Toolbar.accessibility: Use role=toolbar with a name; keep one enabled child at tabindex=0 and skip disabled children.

Checkbox.anatomy: Native checkbox, visible label, grouped options, focus ring, and checked or indeterminate state.
Checkbox.usage: Use for independent choices; use a fieldset and legend when several options share one question.
Checkbox.api: TcCheckbox exposes label, checked, indeterminate, disabled, and change callbacks through tc.ui.checkbox.
Checkbox.accessibility: Keep the native checkbox and visible label; Space toggles it without custom keyboard handling.

Switch.anatomy: Native checkbox with switch role, stable label, truthful state, focus ring, and disabled state.
Switch.usage: Use for an immediate on or off setting, not a pending choice or multi-select.
Switch.api: TcSwitch exposes label, checked, disabled, and change callbacks through tc.ui.switch.
Switch.accessibility: Use a named native checkbox with role=switch; Space toggles it and disabled blocks interaction.

Slider.anatomy: Native range input, visible label, min/max/step constraints, associated output, and focus ring.
Slider.usage: Use for bounded numeric adjustment when the value can be understood from its scale and unit.
Slider.api: TcSlider exposes label, min, max, step, value, disabled, and input callbacks through tc.ui.slider.
Slider.accessibility: Keep the native range and label; arrows change steps while Home and End reach the bounds.

BreakpointProvider.anatomy: Provider context, breakpoint map, and active breakpoint value.
BreakpointProvider.usage: Read the active value for layout and visibility; keep viewport detection in one boundary.
BreakpointProvider.api: TcBreakpointProvider exposes the current breakpoint value and provider scope to descendants.
BreakpointProvider.accessibility: The selector uses focused native buttons and aria-pressed. The detected viewport label is read-only.

Container.anatomy: Available region, constrained inner surface, and centered horizontal padding.
Container.usage: Use a fluid width with a readable maximum; measure the constraint instead of hard-coding page offsets.
Container.api: TcContainer accepts responsive width constraints and centers content within the available region.
Container.accessibility: This is a visual layout surface. Its measured labels explain the constraint and it does not claim interaction.

ScrollToTop.anatomy: Scrollable viewport, scroll position, and an action that returns focus to the viewport top.
ScrollToTop.usage: Use for long content; keep the labeled keyboard action harmless at the top.
ScrollToTop.api: TcScrollToTop exposes a scroll target, a 24px visibility threshold, and smooth return behavior.
ScrollToTop.accessibility: Keep the target focusable; announce position changes and preserve focus after activation.

SwipeArea.anatomy: Gesture surface, current item, previous and next controls, and a live position label.
SwipeArea.usage: Pair touch gestures with visible buttons and keyboard arrows; swiping is never the only content path.
SwipeArea.api: TcSwipeArea exposes index, item count, pointer gesture handling, and previous/next callbacks.
SwipeArea.accessibility: Name the surface, support ArrowLeft/Right, and announce the current item.

FocusTrap.anatomy: Invoker, modal boundary, first and last focusable controls, escape handling, and return target.
FocusTrap.usage: Use only for active modal tasks; cycle Tab inside and restore focus on close.
FocusTrap.api: TcFocusTrap accepts an active state, focusable boundary, escape callback, and restore-focus target.
FocusTrap.accessibility: Use dialog, aria-modal, stable labeling, Tab cycling, Escape, and focus restoration.

Element.anatomy: Semantic tag choice, meaningful content, and the resulting landmark or grouping semantics.
Element.usage: Choose the least powerful semantic element that matches meaning; avoid landmarks for decoration.
Element.api: TcElement renders a selected semantic HTML element while preserving children and required attributes.
Element.accessibility: Semantic structure must match meaning; named navigation regions require an accessible label.

Typography.anatomy: Display scale, body measure, caption style, responsive size, and wrapping or truncation state.
Typography.usage: Use the scale for hierarchy, keep body text readable, and let content wrap before truncating.
Typography.api: TcTypography exposes role, scale, responsive sizing, line height, and overflow behavior.
Typography.accessibility: Preserve heading order, contrast, zoom, and a full or alternate value for truncated text.

Grid.anatomy: Twelve tracks, column gap, and items that occupy explicit spans.
Grid.usage: Place related content on shared tracks and change spans at responsive boundaries.
Grid.api: TcGrid exposes columns, gap, and child span configuration for responsive composition.
Grid.accessibility: The layout selector uses focused native buttons and aria-pressed. Grid content is visual.

Hidden.anatomy: Visibility condition, target content, and the state exposed by the controlling selector.
Hidden.usage: Use it for responsive presence, not for essential information that should be merely visually suppressed.
Hidden.api: TcHidden applies a visibility rule to its child content and preserves the declared breakpoint contract.
Hidden.accessibility: The visibility selector has focus and aria-pressed; hidden content leaves the rendered state.

Divider.anatomy: Horizontal or vertical rule, inset boundary, and optional text label.
Divider.usage: Separate related groups without using color as the only meaning; choose orientation from structure.
Divider.api: TcDivider exposes orientation, inset, and optional label configuration while preserving separator semantics.
Divider.accessibility: Use hr for an unlabeled horizontal rule and separator semantics with aria-orientation for vertical or labeled rules.

Highlighter.anatomy: Safe source text, query field, marked matches, and an announced match count.
Highlighter.usage: Escape source text before marking matches and keep the query visible when no result is found.
Highlighter.api: TcHighlighter accepts source text and query state, producing marked matches without interpreting user text as markup.
Highlighter.accessibility: The query is labeled, the result remains text, and the live match count makes highlighting understandable without color.

Image.anatomy: Responsive frame, local image source, fit mode, loading state, and fallback message.
Image.usage: Provide meaningful alt text, reserve the frame, and use contain when cropping would remove essential context.
Image.api: TcImage exposes source, alt, object-fit, loading, and fallback state for resilient visual content.
Image.accessibility: Alt text describes meaningful content; loading uses status text and fallback names the unavailable image.

Link.anatomy: Accessible link text, valid destination, external indicator, and current or unavailable state.
Link.usage: Keep the text as the accessible name, use a real href, and do not navigate accidentally from demonstration controls.
Link.api: TcLink accepts destination, external, current, and disabled state without converting passive status text into a link.
Link.accessibility: Focus is visible, current uses aria-current, and unavailable content uses aria-disabled without an empty href.

Paper.anatomy: Named surface region, token-driven padding, boundary, tone, and elevation level.
Paper.usage: Use one surface for one meaningful grouping and select outlined, elevated, or tonal treatment by hierarchy.
Paper.api: TcPaper exposes variant and elevation while keeping content width and spacing responsive.
Paper.accessibility: Prefer article or section only for meaningful regions with a heading; otherwise keep the surface presentational.

Skeleton.anatomy: Text, avatar, or card placeholder shapes plus loading and loaded content states.
Skeleton.usage: Reserve the final content geometry, replace placeholders when ready, and respect reduced-motion preferences.
Skeleton.api: TcSkeleton exposes pattern, loading state, and motion policy without leaking decorative fragments to assistive technology.
Skeleton.accessibility: The containing region uses aria-busy and status text; decorative skeleton shapes are aria-hidden.

Autocomplete.anatomy: Text input, filtered listbox, active option, and selection status.
Autocomplete.usage: Filter local choices without hiding the full keyboard path.
Autocomplete.api: TcAutocomplete exposes value, options, filtering, and selection callbacks.
Autocomplete.accessibility: Use combobox/listbox relationships, active descendant state, and announced result counts.

Select.anatomy: Label, native select control, option group, and selection status.
Select.usage: Prefer the native control when the platform picker is sufficient; group related choices.
Select.api: TcSelect exposes value, multiple selection, disabled, and validation state.
Select.accessibility: Associate the label programmatically and expose invalid or disabled states truthfully.

Chips.anatomy: Editable value field, wrapped chip list, remove actions, and live status.
Chips.usage: Use chips for reviewable values; reject empty or duplicate labels before adding them.
Chips.api: TcChips exposes values, add, remove, readonly, disabled, and validation state.
Chips.accessibility: Name each remove action, keep targets at least 40px, and restore focus after removal.

ChipSet.anatomy: Named choice group, native buttons, pressed states, and selection limit feedback.
ChipSet.usage: Use a chip set for a small visible choice set; choose single or multiple mode explicitly.
ChipSet.api: TcChipSet exposes selection mode, pressed values, disabled items, and selection limits.
ChipSet.accessibility: Use native buttons with aria-pressed and a live result; do not present fake radio semantics.

NumericField.anatomy: Labeled number input, min/max/step constraints, step actions, and validation status.
NumericField.usage: Declare bounds and step explicitly; clamp button changes while preserving native text entry.
NumericField.api: TcNumericField exposes value, min, max, step, increment, decrement, and validation state.
NumericField.accessibility: Associate the label and status, announce invalid input, and never rely on color alone.

Radio.anatomy: Fieldset, visible legend, native radio inputs, explicit labels, and a live selection status.
Radio.usage: Use Radio for one choice from a small related set; keep every option labeled and mutually exclusive.
Radio.api: TcRadio exposes value, options, common name, disabled option, and validation state through tc.ui.radio.
Radio.accessibility: Native radios provide Tab, Space, and arrows; the legend names the group and describes errors.

DropZone.anatomy: Visible drop target, labelled multiple file input, drag state, metadata list, and rejection status.
DropZone.usage: Use TcDropZone when dropping is convenient, while keeping browse and keyboard selection equivalent.
DropZone.api: TcDropZone exposes accept, multiple, limits, metadata, and rejection callbacks through tc.ui.drop-zone.
DropZone.accessibility: Pair drag feedback with a focusable input, visible focus, live status, and named actions.

FileUpload.anatomy: Visible file label, native input, selected metadata list, clear action, and validation status.
FileUpload.usage: Use TcFileUpload for local selection; choose single or multiple behavior and validate before upload.
FileUpload.api: TcFileUpload exposes accept, multiple, limits, metadata, and rejection callbacks via tc.ui.file-upload.
FileUpload.accessibility: Keep the input labelled and focusable, announce selection or errors, and name remove actions.

ColorPicker.anatomy: Native color input, explicit label, normalized value text, accessible swatch, and focus ring.
ColorPicker.usage: Use for meaningful colors; keep the native picker and never communicate meaning by color alone.
ColorPicker.api: TcColorPicker exposes label, value, disabled, and callbacks through tc.ui.color-picker.
ColorPicker.accessibility: Use a visible label, native focus, and text beside the swatch.

DatePicker.anatomy: Native date input, label, normalized yyyy-mm-dd value, constraints, feedback, and focus ring.
DatePicker.usage: Use one date with stable boundaries; explain browser/OS display may differ from the normalized value.
DatePicker.api: TcDatePicker exposes value, constraints, disabled, and callbacks through tc.ui.date-picker.
DatePicker.accessibility: Keep the native control, visible label, persistent validity text, and keyboard behavior.

TimePicker.anatomy: Native time input, explicit label, normalized HH:mm value, min/max/step constraints, and feedback.
TimePicker.usage: Use for a time within a same-day range; keep min and max ordered to avoid cross-midnight ambiguity.
TimePicker.api: TcTimePicker exposes value, constraints, disabled, and callbacks through tc.ui.time-picker.
TimePicker.accessibility: Keep the native control, visible label, persistent validity text, and keyboard behavior.

Breadcrumbs.anatomy: Labelled navigation, ordered list, linked ancestors, current page, and hidden separators.
Breadcrumbs.usage: Use for hierarchical wayfinding; keep the current location last and do not fake disabled links.
Breadcrumbs.api: TcBreadcrumbs exposes items, current item, label, separators, and links through tc.ui.breadcrumbs.
Breadcrumbs.accessibility: Use nav, ol, aria-current=page, and aria-hidden separators; preserve logical link order.

Pagination.anatomy: Labelled navigation, ordered page list, previous/next controls, current page, and live status.
Pagination.usage: Use for bounded collections; disable only the unavailable edge control and keep feedback local.
Pagination.api: TcPagination exposes page, page count, labels, edge states, and callbacks through tc.ui.pagination.
Pagination.accessibility: Name the landmark, expose one aria-current=page, label controls, and announce updates.

Tabs.anatomy: Tablist, tabs, selected state, roving tabindex, controlled panels, and live selection status.
Tabs.usage: Use for related preloaded views; activate on click and Left/Right while skipping disabled tabs.
Tabs.api: TcTabs exposes tabs, selected value, disabled items, panels, and callbacks through tc.ui.tabs.
Tabs.accessibility: Pair tab, tabpanel, aria-controls, and aria-labelledby; keep one selected tab and tabindex=0.

AppBar.anatomy: Semantic header, primary context, labelled navigation, disclosure control, and local action.
AppBar.usage: Use for application identity and actions; keep navigation labelled and disclosure state truthful.
AppBar.api: TcAppBar exposes title, actions, navigation, disclosure, and callbacks through tc.ui.app-bar.
AppBar.accessibility: Use labelled header/nav, native controls and links, aria-expanded, aria-controls, and focus.

Drawer.anatomy: Persistent panel, temporary native dialog, visible label, close control, and return focus.
Drawer.usage: Use a persistent panel when context remains; use a modal drawer for temporary navigation.
Drawer.api: TcDrawer exposes mode, label, open state, items, close behavior, and callbacks through tc.ui.drawer.
Drawer.accessibility: Keep persistent content non-modal; use dialog/showModal, Escape, and focus restoration.

NavMenu.anatomy: Labelled nav, nested lists, native links, disclosure button, current page, and local status.
NavMenu.usage: Use site navigation with links and nested groups; collapse only non-essential groups.
NavMenu.api: TcNavMenu exposes label, items, groups, destination, disclosure, and callbacks via tc.ui.nav-menu.
NavMenu.accessibility: Use nav, ul, li, and links rather than menu roles; expose current, expanded, controls.

List.anatomy: Native unordered list, list items, optional secondary text, and native interactive rows.
List.usage: Use for related records; keep passive rows passive and use buttons or links only for real actions.
List.api: TcList exposes items, secondary content, row actions, and selection callbacks via tc.ui.list.
List.accessibility: Use ul and li, keep controls in normal tab order, and announce local actions.

Menu.anatomy: Named menu button, controlled menu, enabled menuitems, disabled item, and restored focus.
Menu.usage: Use for a focused set of actions opened from one button; do not use it for site navigation.
Menu.api: TcMenu exposes actions, disabled items, open state, keyboard behavior, and callbacks via tc.ui.menu.
Menu.accessibility: Use aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, aria-controls, menuitem navigation, and Escape return.

TreeView.anatomy: Tree, nested groups, expandable parents, visible treeitems, selection, and roving focus.
TreeView.usage: Use for nested information; recompute visible nodes after expansion; separate focus from selection.
TreeView.api: TcTreeView exposes nodes, expansion, selection, navigation, and callbacks via tc.ui.tree-view.
TreeView.accessibility: Use tree, treeitem, and group; expose expanded on parents and keep one visible tabindex=0.

Carousel.anatomy: Named region, one visible slide group, manual controls, and polite position status.
Carousel.usage: Use for related items reviewed one at a time; keep rotation manual and wrap at both endpoints.
Carousel.api: TcCarousel exposes items, current index, labels, and previous/next callbacks through tc.ui.carousel.
Carousel.accessibility: Use a meaningful label, named slide groups, hidden inactive slides, and truthful status.

ExpansionPanels.anatomy: Heading-level disclosure buttons, hidden content, independent state, and disabled state.
ExpansionPanels.usage: Use for secondary content that users may open independently; multiple panels can remain expanded.
ExpansionPanels.api: TcExpansionPanels exposes panels, state, disabled items, and callbacks via tc.ui.expansion-panels.
ExpansionPanels.accessibility: Use heading buttons, unique controls, synchronized expanded state, and hidden content.

Avatar.anatomy: Named or decorative initials, optional adjacent name, and visible presence text.
Avatar.usage: Use a meaningful name for informative avatars; hide redundant decoration and group names.
Avatar.api: TcAvatar exposes initials, accessible name, decorative mode, group members, and presence.
Avatar.accessibility: Named informative avatars; aria-hidden decoration; presence is text, not color.

Badge.anatomy: Ordinary text label, contextual count, and optional local update control with polite feedback.
Badge.usage: Keep badges passive; name counts and use status messaging only for real updates.
Badge.api: TcBadge exposes label, count context, tone, and optional update callbacks via tc.ui.badge.
Badge.accessibility: Name counts in text, never rely on color, and do not make a badge an unnecessary button.

Card.anatomy: Article, heading, logical body, native action, and truthful visual state.
Card.usage: Use an article for standalone content; keep actions native and never nest links or buttons.
Card.api: TcCard exposes heading, body, elevation, selected, disabled, and action callbacks via tc.ui.card.
Card.accessibility: Use a real heading and visible focus; visual states need no selection semantics.

Icons.anatomy: Decorative glyph, informative icon, and icon used by a named control.
Icons.usage: Use the local registry; hide redundant glyphs and expose meaning through text or a valid label.
Icons.api: TcIcons exposes token, decorative, label, and fallback properties through tc.ui.icons.
Icons.accessibility: Decorative icons: aria-hidden; informative icons: alternatives; controls: named actions.

Rating.anatomy: Named fieldset, legend, same-name native radios, visible star text, and polite value output.
Rating.usage: Use native radios for one score; label every option and keep targets large enough.
Rating.api: TcRating exposes name, max, value, readOnly, disabled, and change callbacks through tc.ui.rating.
Rating.accessibility: Keyboard radios select; read-only values are text; disabled options stay unavailable.

Alert.anatomy: Visible severity, contextual message, polite status, and explicit urgent error region.
Alert.usage: Use passive status for updates; reserve assertive alerts for urgent user-triggered failures.
Alert.api: TcAlert exposes severity, message, priority, visibility, and update callbacks via tc.ui.alert.
Alert.accessibility: Keep severity visible; use status for updates and alert only after urgent action.

Progress.anatomy: Visible label, native progress, determinate value text, and optional advance control.
Progress.usage: Use progress for completion; provide max/value when known and omit value while indeterminate.
Progress.api: TcProgress exposes label, max, value, indeterminate, disabled, and callbacks via tc.ui.progress.
Progress.accessibility: Use a visible label, repeat value in text, and never use meter for completion.

Dialog.anatomy: Native dialog, visible heading, short description, actions, and focus restoration.
Dialog.usage: Use for a focused task; open with showModal and provide an explicit close action.
Dialog.api: TcDialog exposes open, title, description, actions, return value, and close callbacks.
Dialog.accessibility: Use a labelled heading, contain Tab locally, close on Escape, and restore the opener.

MessageBox.anatomy: Native alertdialog, visible title, message, least-destructive action, and outcome status.
MessageBox.usage: Reserve for interruptive decisions; confirm only the documented local action.
MessageBox.api: TcMessageBox exposes severity, message, confirm, cancel, outcome, and close callbacks.
MessageBox.accessibility: Use alertdialog with aria-modal, name the message, focus the least-destructive action.

Overlay.anatomy: Bounded region, loading layer, busy/inert state, external trigger, and dismiss action.
Overlay.usage: Use for local visual or busy feedback, not as a dialog substitute; keep it bounded.
Overlay.api: TcOverlay exposes scope, active, busy, content, status, dismiss, and completion callbacks.
Overlay.accessibility: Do not claim modal semantics; expose aria-busy, make controlled content inert.

Snackbar.anatomy: Local trigger, separate polite status, hidden message, and optional Undo and Dismiss controls.
Snackbar.usage: Show after a local action; keep recovery reachable without moving focus or auto-dismissing.
Snackbar.api: TcSnackbar exposes message, state, actions, reversal, and dismiss callbacks via tc.ui.snackbar.
Snackbar.accessibility: Announce the message outside controls and preserve logical focus when the surface hides.

Popover.anatomy: Native auto popover, anchored trigger, named informational region, and local status.
Popover.usage: Use for non-modal context; keep essential content persistent and allow native light dismiss.
Popover.api: TcPopover exposes anchor, open state, placement, content, and toggle callbacks via tc.ui.popover.
Popover.accessibility: Use popovertarget, aria-controls, and aria-expanded; never trap focus or claim modality.

Tooltip.anatomy: Named trigger, aria-describedby reference, noninteractive tooltip text, and hidden state.
Tooltip.usage: Use only for supplementary context on hover or focus; keep the text brief and never essential.
Tooltip.api: TcTooltip exposes content, visibility, and dismiss callbacks in tc.ui.tooltip.
Tooltip.accessibility: Use role=tooltip and aria-describedby; keep focus; dismiss on blur or Escape.

DataGrid.anatomy: Named grid, sortable headers, roving cell focus, single row selection, and live status.
DataGrid.usage: Use for small datasets when sorting, cell navigation, and one selected row are useful.
DataGrid.api: TcDataGrid exposes columns, rows, sort, selection, density, and callbacks via tc.ui.data-grid.
DataGrid.accessibility: Use grid semantics, one roving tab stop, aria-sort, aria-selected, and live status.

SimpleTable.anatomy: Native table, column headers, concise records, and local scroll focus region.
SimpleTable.usage: Use for passive small datasets with one header row and no widget-like keyboard behavior.
SimpleTable.api: TcSimpleTable exposes caption, columns, rows, density, and empty state via tc.ui.simple-table.
SimpleTable.accessibility: Use native table semantics, a concise caption, and scope=col for every column header.

Timeline.anatomy: Ordered event list, headings, complete time values, textual status, and one current step.
Timeline.usage: Use for passive chronological sequences whose order and status do not rely on color.
Timeline.api: TcTimeline exposes events, dates, statuses, current step, and density via tc.ui.timeline.
Timeline.accessibility: Use native ol/li, h3 headings, time datetime values, and text for every event status.

BarChart.anatomy: Named bar visual, localized category legend, scale, and equivalent native data table.
BarChart.usage: Use for discrete comparisons; keep labels and units in the data disclosure.
BarChart.api: TcBarChart exposes labels, values, unit, density, and accessible summary via tc.ui.bar-chart.
BarChart.accessibility: Name the visual once and offer the same values in a native table inside details.

DonutChart.anatomy: Named ring visual, completion and remainder labels, percentage, and equivalent data table.
DonutChart.usage: Use for part-to-whole values; expose both segments and their unit in the data disclosure.
DonutChart.api: TcDonutChart exposes labels, values, unit, and summary.
DonutChart.accessibility: Name the visual once and offer every segment value in a native table inside details.

LineChart.anatomy: Named line visual, ordered labels, series values, and equivalent native data table.
LineChart.usage: Use to show change over an ordered dimension; preserve each point and its unit.
LineChart.api: TcLineChart exposes labels, values, unit, and summary.
LineChart.accessibility: Name the trend once and offer every ordered point in a native table inside details.

PieChart.anatomy: Named proportional visual, category legend, percentages, and equivalent native data table.
PieChart.usage: Use for a small set of parts of a whole; expose each segment and its percentage.
PieChart.api: TcPieChart exposes labels, values, unit, density, and accessible summary via tc.ui.pie-chart.
PieChart.accessibility: Name the visual once and offer every value in a native table inside details.

StackedBarChart.anatomy: Named stacked visual, category rows, separate series, totals, and equivalent data table.
StackedBarChart.usage: Use to compare composition and totals; keep every stacked series separately available.
StackedBarChart.api: TcStackedBarChart exposes rows, series, totals, and summary.
StackedBarChart.accessibility: Name the visual once and expose each series value in a native table inside details.

Field.anatomy: Label, input, helper description, required state, and visible validation state.
Field.usage: Use as the shared field contract for labeled values and local supporting text.
Field.api: Field is the shared validation contract implemented by public controls such as TcTextField and TcSwitch.
Field.accessibility: Use label/aria-describedby, native constraints, text validation, and visible focus.

Form.anatomy: Native form, validated fields, submit and reset controls, and local result summary.
Form.usage: Use for local validation; do not imply network submission or persistence.
Form.api: Form is a native form coordinated by attachFormValidation(nativeForm, options); it is not a TcForm tag.
Form.accessibility: Describe fields/errors, expose a live summary, focus first invalid, and reset.

TextField.anatomy: Native text or email input, label, autocomplete, description, and readable error state.
TextField.usage: Use for one-line text; choose type and autocomplete from the expected value.
TextField.api: TcTextField exposes value, type, autocomplete, required, readOnly, disabled, and validation.
TextField.accessibility: Associate label/description, expose aria-invalid, and keep errors readable.

Table.anatomy: Native table, column and row headers, textual status, and local scrolling.
Table.usage: Use for passive relational data where each row needs a meaningful first-column header.
Table.api: TcTable exposes caption, columns, rows, row headers, density, and state via tc.ui.table.
Table.accessibility: Use native semantics and scope=col/scope=row; status must not rely on color.

Button.overview: A native command with one clear intent.
Button.variants: Compare primary, secondary, ghost, and destructive emphasis.
Button.states: Disabled controls cannot activate; loading remains unavailable until work completes.

ButtonFab.overview: A compact contextual action with a visible focus target.
ButtonFab.variants: Compare circular, filled, and extended floating actions.
ButtonFab.states: The disabled FAB stays named and visible but cannot activate.

ButtonGroup.overview: Related actions share a named context and native tab order.
ButtonGroup.variants: Compare grouped navigation actions with one emphasized choice.
ButtonGroup.states: Each member remains an independent native action in DOM order.

IconButton.overview: A compact named action for familiar icon commands.
IconButton.variants: Compare favorite, edit, and unavailable commands.
IconButton.states: Unavailable commands keep their names and remain inactive.

ToggleIconButton.overview: A compact named action with an explicit pressed state.
ToggleIconButton.variants: Compare the off and on states without changing the label.
ToggleIconButton.states: Keyboard and pointer activation update the state and live output.

Toolbar.overview: A named horizontal command surface with one Tab stop.
Toolbar.variants: Compare icon commands, mixed commands, and wrapping.
Toolbar.states: Arrow navigation skips disabled commands and wraps safely.

demo.fileTypes: PDF, PNG, or ZIP · up to 25 MB
demo.actualViewportDetail: Detected from the browser width; this is not simulated.
demo.simulatedViewportDetail: Use the focused selector to preview provider output without changing the viewport.
demo.providerStateDetail: The active label follows the current browser width.

buildStatus.title: Build status
buildStatus.intro: This page is the in-product source of truth for the documentation stage. Counts explain coverage; they do not imply production readiness.
buildStatus.stage1Detail: The information architecture and canonical component routes are complete.
buildStatus.stage2: Bilingual documentation, semantic icons, charts, responsive foundations, catalog layout, and visual foundations
buildStatus.stage2Detail: Visuals and five Inputs/Forms slices passed; details pending; WU-03 not started.
buildStatus.responsiveStandard: Every component batch must verify widths 390, 768/800, 1024, 1280, 1440, 1920, and 2560; wrapping related actions; zero document-root and sidebar horizontal overflow without blanket clipping; comfortable/compact computed spacing; centered article/TOC allocation; and minimum 40px visible button, navigation, and control targets. Icon, chart, and responsive-foundation batches remain documentation work; WU-03 is not started.
buildStatus.stage3Detail: Explicitly not started in this prototype stage.
buildStatus.categoriesDetail: Foundations/Layout, Actions, Inputs/Forms, Navigation/Disclosure, Surfaces/Content, Feedback/Overlays, Data/Visualization.
buildStatus.iconsDetail: The local metadata contains 3,975 unique codepoints; tokens and codepoints are different measures.
buildStatus.localesDetail: Both locale files are structurally isomorphic and loaded locally.
buildStatus.accordion: Removed accordion-based hiding so core documentation stays visible.
buildStatus.docs: Expanded component docs with six sections, direct routes, demos, variants, and states.
buildStatus.iconCorrection: Corrected icon metadata handling and preserved the local font and token explorer.
buildStatus.bilingual: Added complete English/Spanish content architecture and synchronized README pair.
buildStatus.checkRoutes: Validate every component route in both locales.
buildStatus.checkIcons: Validate local icon search, five matrices, and 24 practical combinations.
buildStatus.checkRuntime: Validate runtime, accessibility labels, local assets, routes, and responsive widths.
buildStatus.nextBoundaryText: Production WU-03 is not part of this prototype stage.

components.BreakpointProvider: Defines responsive breakpoints so layouts adapt predictably across viewport sizes.
components.Container: Constrains content width while preserving a responsive layout boundary.
components.Divider: Separates related content with a clear visual and semantic boundary.
components.Element: Provides a semantic surface primitive for composing accessible content.
components.FocusTrap: Keeps keyboard focus within an active surface until the interaction is complete.
components.Grid: Arranges content in a consistent responsive column and row system.
components.Hidden: Conditionally hides content at defined breakpoints without changing the layout contract.
components.Highlighter: Emphasizes matching text while preserving readable surrounding content.
components.Image: Displays visual content with predictable sizing, fitting, and fallback behavior.
components.Link: Connects destinations with an explicit navigation meaning and visible affordance.
components.Paper: Provides an elevation surface for grouping content and establishing hierarchy.
components.ScrollToTop: Returns a long content view to its starting position with a clear action.
components.Skeleton: Communicates loading structure before the final content is available.
components.SwipeArea: Defines a touch-friendly region for horizontal navigation and gesture feedback.
components.Typography: Establishes readable type scale, rhythm, hierarchy, and supporting metadata.
components.Button: Presents a clear action with emphasis, intent, and loading feedback.
components.ButtonFab: Presents a compact floating action that can expand into an optional text action.
components.ButtonGroup: Groups related actions while making their relationship and selection clear.
components.IconButton: Presents a compact icon-only action with an accessible name and state.
components.ToggleIconButton: Toggles one icon action between explicit pressed and unpressed states.
components.Toolbar: Groups frequent contextual actions into a compact, predictable command surface.
components.Autocomplete: Suggests matching values while the user enters text into a constrained field.
components.Checkbox: Captures independent boolean choices with clear checked and indeterminate states.
components.Chips: Represents compact input, filter, or assist values that can be selected or dismissed.
components.ChipSet: Coordinates a collection of chips with a defined selection and dismissal model.
components.ColorPicker: Helps users choose a color through recognizable visual and textual inputs.
components.DatePicker: Captures a date or date range through a navigable calendar interaction.
components.DropZone: Accepts files through a visible drag-and-drop boundary and validation feedback.
components.Field: Provides a shared contract for labels, helper text, validation, and value states.
components.FileUpload: Collects files with explicit type, size, progress, and recovery feedback.
components.Form: Coordinates validated fields and exposes a visible submission outcome.
components.NumericField: Captures numeric values with constraints, formatting, and step behavior.
components.Radio: Selects one option from a related set with a clear group relationship.
components.Select: Chooses one or more values from a visible, keyboard-operable option list.
components.Slider: Adjusts a value or range along a bounded continuous or discrete scale.
components.Switch: Expresses an immediate on or off setting with a persistent state.
components.TextField: Captures labeled text with validation, affordances, and readable states.
components.TimePicker: Captures a time through clock, keyboard, and format-aware interactions.
components.AppBar: Anchors primary context and actions in a consistent application header.
components.Breadcrumbs: Shows the current location within a navigable hierarchy.
components.Carousel: Presents related items one at a time with visible position and navigation controls.
components.Drawer: Provides persistent or modal navigation while preserving the main content context.
components.ExpansionPanels: Reveals grouped secondary content with an explicit expansion state.
components.List: Presents related records in a scannable, optionally interactive sequence.
components.Menu: Presents a focused set of actions with keyboard and pointer navigation.
components.NavMenu: Structures application destinations into a clear, composable navigation model.
components.Pagination: Moves through a bounded collection with visible position and adjacent controls.
components.Tabs: Switches between related views while preserving a clear selected state.
components.TreeView: Represents nested information with expandable hierarchy and selection affordances.
components.Avatar: Represents a person or entity through initials, imagery, and status context.
components.Badge: Adds concise status, count, or attention context to another surface.
components.Card: Groups one understandable decision or content summary inside a bounded surface.
components.Icons: Provides a consistent icon presentation primitive for symbolic interface meaning.
components.Rating: Communicates a quantitative or qualitative score with a recognizable scale.
components.Alert: Communicates persistent contextual information that may require user attention.
components.Dialog: Presents a focused decision surface with predictable open, close, and focus behavior.
components.MessageBox: Frames a concise message and decision with an explicit severity and action.
components.Overlay: Places a temporary visual layer above content while defining interaction boundaries.
components.Popover: Anchors contextual content to a triggering control without losing page context.
components.Progress: Communicates completion, activity, or indeterminate work at a glance.
components.Snackbar: Reports a transient result with an optional recovery or undo action.
components.Tooltip: Explains an unfamiliar control or value at the moment it needs context.
components.BarChart: Compares values across categories with a readable visual scale.
components.DataGrid: Presents structured data with headers, selection, loading, and empty states.
components.DonutChart: Shows part-to-whole relationships with a central visual balance.
components.LineChart: Shows change over an ordered dimension through connected data points.
components.PieChart: Shows proportional categories through a bounded circular composition.
components.SimpleTable: Presents a compact set of rows and columns for quick comparison.
components.StackedBarChart: Compares totals and composition across categories in one visual scale.
components.Table: Presents relational data with stable headers, rows, and state feedback.
components.Timeline: Shows ordered events with time, status, and progression context.
